info.title: What is Forest Bathing?
info.lead: Forest Bathing, or “Shinrin-yoku”, is the practice of spending slow, deliberate time in the forest with all five senses open. It is not a hike to conquer a summit — it is stopping, listening, smelling, touching, and letting the forest do its work on your body and mind.

points.title: Walk slowly
points.desc: Short distances over a long time. The point is what you notice, not how far you go.

points.title: Open your senses
points.desc: Listen to the forest, smell the soil and leaves, feel the bark and the wind.

points.title: Guided throughout
points.desc: A facilitator leads you through activities that connect you with nature along the way.

locations.title: Choose your forest
locations.lead: Each place offers a different experience. Pick a location to see its open dates.

chet-kot.name: Chet Kot – Pong Kon Sao National Park
chet-kot.blurb: Forest inside a national park, about two hours from Bangkok. An overnight trip.

doi-tung.name: Doi Tung
doi-tung.blurb: Highland watershed forest in Chiang Rai. Cool year-round, with natural walking trails.

urban-bangkok.name: EXPLORE THE ORIGINAL ART OF FOREST BATHING
urban-bangkok.region: Chaloem Phrakiat 80 Phansa Park, Khung Bang Kachao, Samut Prakan
urban-bangkok.blurb: Breathe with the forest. A mindful morning of Japanese forest bathing at Bang Krachao — Bangkok's green lung. Slow down, reconnect, and leave feeling lighter.

info.title: Guided Breathwork
info.desc: Start with slow, guided breathing to settle the mind before entering the forest trail.

info.title: Sensory Walk
info.desc: A slow walk through Bang Krachao's green canopy, engaging all five senses along the way.

info.title: Tea Ceremony
info.desc: Close the session with a quiet tea ceremony under the trees, reflecting on the morning.

info.title: Who it's for
info.desc: No fitness level required. The whole route is flat and slow-paced, suitable for children from age 10 and for anyone new to forest bathing. Come alone or bring someone — most people arrive on their own and leave having shared something with the group.

info.title: What you'll take home
info.desc: A simple set of practices you can repeat in any green space near you: how to slow your pace deliberately, how to notice what your senses pick up, and how to let a short walk actually reset your attention rather than just move your body.

location.address: Bang Krachao pier, Phra Pradaeng, Samut Prakarn
location.gettingThere: Bang Krachao sits directly across the river from Khlong Toei. From BTS Bang Na take a taxi to Wat Klong Phra Udom pier (about 20 minutes), then the cross-river boat runs every few minutes. If you drive, park at the pier — parking is free and the boat takes you and your bicycle across.

items.title: Meet at the pier, cross the river together

prepare: A light rain jacket — the session runs rain or shine
includes: A certified forest bathing facilitator for the whole session
Full refund if you cancel at least 7 days ahead

reviews.name: Nathan K.
